# THE IMPORTERS THIS ENGINE SHIPS — one NAMED ROW each, and the count is derived from the rows.
#
# WHY A REGISTER AND NOT A NUMBER. A gate that pins "assimp offers N formats" is satisfied by editing N,
# which is the shape this project has paid for before: the register is the rows, and the count is read off
# them. Adding an importer means adding a row WITH ITS REASON here; nothing else in the tree names a format.
#
# WHO READS THIS FILE, and it is deliberately more than one reader:
#   * BuildScripts/ThirdParty/Assimp.lua — takes the FULL list of formats from assimp's own
#     code/CMakeLists.txt (`ADD_ASSIMP_IMPORTER( NAME )`) and defines ASSIMP_BUILD_NO_<NAME>_IMPORTER for
#     every format that is NOT named below. A format assimp adds in a future version is therefore OFF by
#     default rather than silently shipped.
#   * Desert/Tests/Editor/AssimpBoundary — asserts that the extensions the BUILT library reports through
#     aiGetImportFormatDescription() are exactly the extensions below. That is the half a build file
#     cannot state: the defines say what we asked for, the library says what we got.
#
# Columns: NAME (assimp's own macro name)  |  extensions, space separated, lower case, no dot  |  reason.
#
FBX   fbx        The editor's own import path and FbxMeshSplitter both read FBX; base.fbx is the corpus.
OBJ   obj        FbxMeshSplitter WRITES .obj and the editor reads it back, so dropping it breaks a round trip.
GLTF  gltf glb vrm   The interchange format the engine is expected to accept from outside tools. The
#                     `vrm` is NOT a choice of ours: assimp's glTF2 importer claims it alongside gltf/glb,
#                     and this column records what the BUILT LIBRARY reports, read off a run rather than
#                     predicted. Removing it here would make the census red without changing what ships.
